items.stem: A list page issues one query for parents and then one query per parent for its children. This is:

options.rationale: Correct: one query plus N child queries is the classic N+1 problem.
A deadlock is mutual lock waiting, not repeated queries.
It is a well-known performance anti-pattern.
No rollback is implied by the pattern.

items.explanation: Correct: one query plus N child queries is the classic N+1 problem.

items.stem: Accessing a LAZY association after the transaction has closed typically causes:

options.rationale: Correct: lazy loading needs an open persistence context; outside it, it fails.

options.text: A successful silent load from the database
options.rationale: There is no session to load from once the context is closed.
It is a runtime error, not a compile-time one.
Fetch type does not change automatically at access time.

items.explanation: Correct: lazy loading needs an open persistence context; outside it, it throws LazyInitializationException.

items.stem: Which TWO are sound ways to resolve an N+1 problem? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use a fetch join in the query
options.rationale: Correct: a fetch join loads the association in one query.

options.text: Use an entity graph to specify what to fetch
options.rationale: Correct: entity graphs declare eager fetching for a specific query.
Global EAGER causes over-fetching and new performance problems.
Disabling transactions does not address the query count and harms correctness.

items.explanation: Correct: fetch joins and entity graphs both resolve N+1 without the harms of global EAGER.
